items.title: What's driving seller confidence in 2026
items.description: What's driving seller confidence in 2026 by Elizabeth Kanzeg Rowland November 23, 2026 Sellers put in the research to understand pricing and mortgage rates, leading to higher levels of confidence in the selling process. Uncertain rate outlooks and affordability concerns failed to dampen seller confidence in 2026, according to a new Ipsos study commissioned by Century 21 Real Estate. The group's Home Seller Confidence Report revealed high levels of confidence as sellers balance optimal pricing with the emotional drivers behind a move. Over 1,000 Americans over the age of 21 who were current, prospective or recent home sellers were interviewed for the study. So what's driving the trend? Sellers who prioritize strategy, researchers noted. Secure sellers Sellers have few qualms about selling in today's market conditions. Among homeowners planning to sell within 12 months, 75% believe now is the right time to move. So do 82% of those whose homes were already listed. Seller confidence may be age-dependent, researchers found. A substantial 83% of sellers aged 21 to 34 expressed confidence that now is the right time to sell. Meanwhile, sellers aged 35 to 54 and sellers aged 55-plus reported confidence at rates of 78% and 58%, respectively. What's moving movers? Mortgage rates influenced sellers' actions, but personal incentives drove decisions too. Of sellers interviewed, 86% said their mortgage rate was slightly, moderately, very or extremely influential on the timing of their move. Giving up an auspicious mortgage rate created a pain point for many sellers, with 63% of sellers with a mortgage rate below 5% stating that giving up their rate was emotionally difficult and 54% of all sellers agreeing that giving up their rate was harder than leaving their home. Around 19% of sellers listed mortgage rates as their top reason for moving. But personal reasons were given more often, like change of scenery (27%), finding their next home (25%), a personal life event (22%) and feeling emotionally ready (21%). “Mortgage rates are a big part of the housing conversation, but people don't make decisions about their homes based on rates alone,” said Mike Miedler, president and CEO of Century 21 Real Estate. “New jobs, growing families and other life changes still motivate people to move. Sellers aren't waiting for perfect conditions, but they are approaching that decision with more thought and preparation. They want to understand what their home is worth and how quickly it could sell so they can move forward with confidence.” The pricing problem Many sellers expressed concern over getting the best possible price for their home. This priority became especially pronounced with older sellers. Almost half (47%) of sellers 55-plus listed getting the highest possible sales price as the most important outcome when selling their home. This percentage dropped to 32% for sellers aged 35 to 54 and just 16% for sellers aged 21 to 34. Uncertainty about proper pricing led 58% of all sellers to worry about pricing too high and 27% to worry about pricing too low. Notably, 66% of sellers who sold in the last 24 months seriously reconsidered or changed their asking price before listing — some over four times. Of this cohort, however, 35% never ended up changing the price at all throughout the selling process. Where sellers turn In response to uncertainties like pricing, sellers seek information and guidance. Some look to real estate professionals. The study found that agents have influence over seller pricing decisions. Of sellers who listed with an agent, 59% followed their agent’s pricing recommendation. Other sellers turned to AI, with 54% of sellers saying that AI gave them significantly or somewhat more confidence while selling their home. Around 67% of recent and prospective sellers used AI for tasks like estimating home values, studying local market conditions and researching where to move next. However, many sellers recognized AI's limitations, especially when it came to providing pricing accuracy instead of placating with optimistic estimates. For sellers who compared an agent's recommendation with an AI pricing estimate, 45% reported that their agent was closer to their final sale price. Overall, 46% of those who compared AI and their agent’s pricing advice trusted the agent more, while just 15% trusted AI more. The big picture Strategy and security drive seller choices. Sellers put in the research to understand pricing and mortgage rates, leading to higher levels of confidence in the selling process. “Today's sellers are approaching one of life's biggest financial decisions with more research and intention than ever before,” said Miedler. “They're exploring pricing strategies, evaluating buyer demand and looking for trusted guidance before bringing their homes to market. The sellers who feel most confident are often the ones who have a clear strategy from the start.” Read More Related to This Post October pending home sales could represent bottom of cycle Bleak house: Builder confidence hits 14-year low in November Existing-home sales miss estimates in October Housing affordability improves quarterly, annually in Houston Cotality: Northeast, Midwest drive US home-price growth in September New construction and affordability determine Houston’s hottest communities in Q3 Houston leads the nation in millionaire renter growth Home prices rise in majority of Texas metros but decrease statewide Join the conversation Cancel reply Save my name, email, and website in this browser for the next time I comment.

items.title: EXCLUSIVE: Steven Spielberg’s L.A. Ranch Sells for $8 Million Below Asking—Just 2 Months After Hitting the Market
items.description: Filmmaker Steven Spielberg has sold the sprawling Los Angeles ranch where he housed his horses for $22.3 million—just two months after listing the palatial estate. Spielberg, 79, and his wife, Kate Capshaw , 72, purchased the property in 1999 through their corporate entity, Texas Tart, for $5.75 million. They listed the massive compound in September for $30 million. Then, in late October, the home disappeared from the market with no indication why. Now, Realtor.com® can exclusively reveal that the property has traded hands, selling for $22.3 million—at a nearly $8 million discount. When they purchased the home, the Hollywood mogul and actress unveiled ambitious plans to dramatically overhaul the estate with a 27,000-square-foot, five-story riding facility featuring a domed roof and underground horse stables. Spielberg's vision reportedly included more than $7 million in renovations, as well as plans to construct a 2,400-square-foot guesthouse and a three-story guardhouse. Loading... Filmmaker Steven Spielberg has sold the sprawling Los Angeles ranch where he housed his horses for $22.3 million—just two months after listing the palatial estate. Presley Ann/Getty Images for Lucas Museum of Narrative Art However, neighbors objected to the scale of the project. While the Oscar-winning director reportedly planned to present revised ideas to his neighbors, the elaborate project ultimately never came to fruition. Meanwhile, he did update the estate into the magnificent abode it is today. The property was held by Spielberg and Capshaw for nearly three decades. Last month, the couple decided to finally part ways with the equestrian retreat, listing it for $29.9 million with Sandro Dazzan of The Agency. Known as Dogwood, the seven-bedroom, 9.5-bathroom estate sits on 2.8 acres in the secluded Sullivan Canyon. It offers an impressive array of equestrian amenities alongside its luxurious living spaces. "Nestled in the ultra-private Sullivan Canyon, Dogwood is Los Angeles' premiere equestrian ranch—a rare masterpiece designed by renowned architect Michael Kovac with interiors by Michael Smith and landscape design by Christine London ," the listing stated. Spanning two parcels, the property combines a sophisticated country-inspired aesthetic with extensive facilities designed for horses, entertaining, and guests. Inside the main residence, rich walnut floors and wood-covered ceilings create a warm atmosphere, while expansive windows bring in plenty of natural light. The spacious living room offers multiple seating areas anchored by dual fireplaces, creating an inviting space for relaxing and entertaining. That rustic aesthetic continues into the chef's kitchen, which features extensive wood cabinetry, an oversized center island, high-end appliances, and an eat-in dining nook. "The chef's kitchen with eat-in dining nook and wood-burning fireplace connects to a cozy family room and IPE-clad terrace overlooking a tranquil reflection pond," the listing noted. Upstairs, the primary suite offers a peaceful retreat complete with a wood-burning fireplace and access to a private covered terrace. Loading... Spielberg, 79, and his wife, Kate Capshaw, 72, purchased the property in 1999 through their corporate entity, Texas Tart, for $5.75 million. Tristan Fewings/Getty Images for BFI The outdoor space boasts yet another fireplace along with sweeping city and canyon views, according to the listing. Elsewhere inside the home is a media room that can double as a game room, as well as a wine cellar. But the property's most impressive features are arguably those designed for its four-legged residents. Across from the main entertaining spaces sits a six-stall barn complete with an executive office, staff quarters, three grooming stations, a feed kitchen, and storage. The equestrian facility is topped off by a sprawling 20,000-square-foot riding arena with an observation deck and mirrored wall, which the listing notes is suitable for both dressage and jumping. The estate's lower parcel expands the compound with a stylish one-bedroom guesthouse equipped with its own kitchen, rooftop deck, and basement office and storage spaces. There is also a second four-stall barn, a 5,400-square-foot turnout area, a private gate, and parking for more than 10 vehicles. Both parcels are supported by a security command post and generators. The ranch is surrounded by lush landscaping, while a tranquil reflection pond adds to its secluded, countryside atmosphere—despite the estate's location in the heart of Los Angeles. With this $29.9 million listing, Spielberg and Capshaw are closing a decades-long chapter. Even without having resided in this property, the couple aren't short on lavish abodes to call home. Their main residence is a stunning Pacific Palisades abode, which has served as their home since 1985. The property spans 20,000 square feet and boasts a media room, a 14,000-gallon aquarium, and several other lavish amenities. Over in Malibu, they own a beachfront abode, which is made up of two parcels. They purchased the first parcel in 1989 for $3.3 million and the second in 2000 for $3.2 million. Loading... Now, Realtor.com can exclusively reveal that the property has traded hands, selling for $22.3 million—at a nearly $8 million discount. Michael Loccisano/Getty Images The home is situated on a 1.44-acre lot and boasts 144 feet of ocean frontage. They also hold the keys to a dwelling in New York , which they purchased in 1983. The couple snapped up the 6-acre estate and enlisted architect Charles Gwathmey to overhaul the abode. Over the years, he added horse stables and a lavish guesthouse. In 2008, he expanded the property by picking up a 3.2-acre pond in the front of the home for $20 million. Also on the East Coast, the couple own a 6,000-square-foot apartment building in Manhattan. items.title: For D Magazine Editors, It's All About the Blurbs
items.description: Live Poll As we headed to press with the December issue of the magazine, our dining critic, Brian Reinhart, had a lot on his—get ready for it—plate. (I apologize.) Not only did the subject of his lead review shutter, forcing him to rewrite his story under duress, but online he was breaking international news and fulfilling the media requests that said news generated. Brian figured out that the Michelin tire company used AI to write the blurbs for the five Dallas restaurants it recently added to its famous guide. Google “Brian Reinhart figured out Michelin used AI.” You’ll find what I’m talking about. I should add that a Michelin spokesperson denied that AI was used to write their blurbs. And then I should further add that I don’t believe that spokesperson. This might surprise you, but I feel bad for Michelin. Clarification: I don’t feel bad for the $26 billion multinational company but rather the folks who run the tiny corner of its operation called the Michelin Guide. They employ writers, whom they call Inspectors with a capital “I,” and whom they do not identify. I am considering a title change for everyone on the D Magazine staff. Wouldn’t it be better for everyone if we were Quartermasters? Anyway, the Inspectors have a difficult job. They have to write blurbs about restaurants. I hate writing blurbs. For our “Best of Big D” feature , everyone on staff has to pitch in (with help from freelancers, too). Our blurbs are 50 words, plus or minus. I’m always the last Quartermaster to turn in his blurbs because I am given to procrastinate when it comes to hard tasks I don’t enjoy. Writing BoBD blurbs tests every Quartermaster’s skills to make a forceful, informative argument in 50 words as to why a restaurant or media outlet or park has risen above the rest. It takes time and talent. It takes personal experience. It takes care. And it takes integrity. Guides The Best of Big D Winners 2026 We're letting you in on all our Dallas aces. items.description: Live Poll Five years ago this week, the Rangers committed more than $560 million to free agents in a span of less than 48 hours. In an echo of the Alex Rodriguez signing two decades earlier, most of it went to a splashy new middle infield duo, Corey Seager (10 years, $325 million) and Marcus Semien (seven years, $175 million). The instant investment, just before an impending lockout, signaled the starting point for a new era. It brought a sort of gravity to the previously downtrodden Rangers, drawing scrutiny, pressure and, ultimately, more stars. For the first time in a long time, the Rangers were back to their big-spending ways. Before long, they’d have a World Series to show for it. Now, five years later, another lockout looms on the heels of another disappointing Rangers season. This time, there is no optimism in Texas. Semien is gone. Seager, like several of his teammates, is the subject of trade rumors. The latest era of Rangers prosperity already seems like it’s over. Money spent starts out hypothetical: big upward lines on charts. It ends up cold and complicated, black and white cells scrolling by on a spreadsheet. In the moment, the spending was supposed to accelerate the team’s trajectory, according to then-president of baseball operations Jon Daniels’ recollection . It was supposed to spark fan excitement. Halfway through Seager and Semien’s foundational deals, it’s becoming clear what the money did and didn’t buy. First, it’s important to remember where the Rangers stood prior to their spending. When Seager and Semien signed on, Texas was coming off a 60-102 season, their first with actual fans populating Globe Life Field, the ballpark that opened during the COVID-19 pandemic. Daniels, architect of the 2010 and 2011 pennant winners, was in charge, but Chris Young had been added as general manager. The Rangers hadn’t made the postseason or managed a .500 record since 2016, and a few months earlier they had made a rebuild-focused move in trading Joey Gallo to the Yankees. Reliever José Leclerc was the only player on the roster owed a guaranteed contract. The hope on hand was bubbling up in top prospect Josh Jung, recent draftee Jack Leiter, and the Costco-style bulk buy acquired for Gallo (including future super utilityman Ezequiel Duran), but proven major-league contributors were few and far between. New had to be better, because new was the whole plan. So, with a labor stoppage looming, in came Seager and Semien, along with starting pitcher Jon Gray and veteran outfielder Kole Calhoun. The immediate results were terrible. Seager had a down year offensively, batting just .245. Gray was average. Calhoun was unplayable. The kids took their lumps, as they’re prone to do. Ownership fired Daniels and manager Chris Woodward before the team limped home with a 68-94 record. Undeterred by sign-stealing shame, the Astros won the World Series. But investment has influence beyond just what it pays for. There was commitment baked into the expenditure. Young, elevated to top baseball executive, moved aggressively again to help the original spend pay off in the winter of 2022. In came Jacob deGrom and Nathan Eovaldi and Andrew Heaney. More importantly, in came Bruce Bochy. Out went what it cost to bolster a fresh, competitive team at the trade deadline. When the Rangers clinched the first World Series in franchise history the following summer, with the crack of Seager’s bat and the roar of his primal scream echoing from days before, Young talked about how they got there. “Corey and Marcus, they believed in us at a time they didn’t have to,” Young told USA Today . “I’m so happy they’ve been rewarded. It was just the start. We couldn’t stop. We were sick of losing. Our players were sick of losing.” Maybe the spending amortized itself that night in Arlington, any remaining expectations blown up and mixed in with the confetti. A great many baseball teams have paid more for less satisfying outcomes. For so long, Texas was among them. In the aftermath of the title, the Rangers essentially did stop. Spending has slowed to a drip. The club drifted back not to losing, but to that frustrating level between losing and winning . As the champagne buzz gradually wore off, the results stayed flat. With payroll set to remain as is, ownership seems to be broadly OK with all of that. A slower pace brings the opportunity for contemplation. And if it is indeed time to tabulate the final results of that frenzied spending five years ago, some numbers are easy to check. Like whether the Rangers signed the right stars. items.title: Human review remains paramount for AI mortgage underwriting
items.description: Artificial intelligence is helping mortgage lenders and due-diligence firms review loan files and extract borrower information, but integrating AI into underwriting processes isn't a one-and-done experience. The technology still needs human oversight, experts say, especially when loans involve unusual circumstances or require judgment beyond standard guidelines. At Incenter Diligence Solutions , AI has accelerated document indexing and data extraction, according to president Pamela Hamrick. Technology can now sort and categorize thousands of pages of loan documents in minutes, replacing a process that once required employees to manually separate and label files. Hamrick said that while AI can extract information from standardized mortgage documents like loan estimates and closing disclosures, borrower-provided records — including pay stubs and bank statements. — are harder to process because their formats vary. AI, however, can identify inconsistencies across documents and summarize them for underwriters to investigate. "The technology is identifying the questions, and the inconsistencies and the anomalies, between all of this documentation, and summarizing that for an underwriter or a reviewer … to dig deeper and make a decision about whether or not what the AI has identified is a real risk — or if it's a minimal risk or maybe it's no risk at all because of the particular scenario," Hamrick said in an interview with HousingWire . Secondary market effects Julia Curran , senior managing director of residential AI products at SitusAMC , said the company uses AI to re-underwrite closed loans in the secondary market, checking regulatory and underwriting guidelines as well as data accuracy before loans are reviewed for securitization . According to Curran, SitusAMC builds AI agents around processes established by human subject matter experts and tests their results against loans previously reviewed by people. She said the company runs repeated tests until the system reaches at least 95% accuracy. But the technology still needs the human touch. Curran said the system sends blank or inconsistent fields to human reviewers, and final credit decisions require judgments that cannot be reduced to individual data points. "A final credit decision shouldn't be made by the machine because there's other things to consider besides the specific data points," Curran said. Hamrick added: "Companies that fully rely on AI are potentially going to have misses in some other areas where a human might have been able to make a different decision.” Curran also warned about the AI model supplying information not supported or provided by the documents submitted. She described a case in which a model supplied a solar panel number that was not included in a particular loan file. The answer was correct, but the system had apparently drawn on information from other files. "Even though it's right, I don't want that answer," Curran said. "I want to stay within the four walls of this file." Testing adds time and cost The executives said lenders should test AI against established human processes before relying on it for underwriting. Hamrick recommended introducing the technology in one part of the workflow at a time, comparing its results with human reviews before expanding its use. She also said lenders should prepare employees for changes by retraining them for tasks that require more human intervention. "The best thing that we can do as leaders is look where the technology can ultimately take over, and then take the folks that are doing those roles and train them to be better at the things that require more human intervention," she said. Curran said quality control requires testing models across different loan types and scenarios. SitusAMC maintains a test bank of hundreds of previously reviewed loans, including purchases, refinances, adjustable-rate mortgages and loans with rate buydowns. When a model changes, the company runs its prompts against the test bank to check whether results remain consistent. These tests add costs that lenders may overlook. Curran said companies should ask AI vendors how their systems were developed, whether subject matter experts helped establish the processes and whether ongoing regression testing is in place. "You want the same answer every time," Curran said. "The process of taking a non-deterministic process and making it deterministic takes a lot of time and effort.” Related More: Artificial Intelligence quality control Underwriting

items.title: Washington state regulator issues temporary stop on new business for Directors Mortgage
items.description: The Washington Department of Financial Institutions (DFI) has ordered Directors Mortgage to temporarily stop taking on new business in the state, including the origination of loans for Washington residents or for properties located in the state, citing exam interference and concerns about the company’s finances. According to the DFI’s order, examiners who conducted an on-site review at the Oregon-based lender’s main office from Nov. 17 to Nov. 19 were not provided requested information and records. During that period, the department served a subpoena on the company’s CEO and owner to obtain the production of original books, accounts, papers, records and files. The department also said it obtained information during the examination indicating that the company was not meeting its financial obligations to employees or third-party vendors. “Respondent’s failure to comply with the Department’s examination authority and Respondent’s current financial condition pose a serious risk of injury to the public,” the order states. A representative of Directors Mortgage did not immediately respond to HousingWire ’s request for comment. The emergency order, signed on Friday by Brian J. Guerard, Washington DFI’s acting director, requires Directors Mortgage to deliver detailed financial information, including balance sheets and bank account data, and to fully respond to the department’s subpoena. The order also directs the company to satisfy outstanding financial obligations. Under Washington law, companies may contest such orders in an administrative hearing. If a respondent does not seek a hearing, the order becomes permanent when DFI issues a final order. Directors Mortgage, founded in 1998 by president and CEO Mark J. Hanna and headquartered in Oregon, has originated about $235 million in mortgages year to date, according to InGenius . The company had roughly 40 loan officers and nine active branches as of Monday, per data from the Nationwide Multistate Licensing System . Washington’s DFI has been active recently regarding mortgage enforcement. Newrez recently agreed to pay roughly $3 million and implement wide-ranging mortgage servicing changes to resolve allegations by the department that it engaged in unfair or deceptive acts or practices. Earlier this year, Washington state regulators issued a $75,000 fine and a $3,000 investigation fee against West Capital Lending , alleging multiple violations of the state's consumer loan act. The company was accused of allowing unlicensed individuals to conduct mortgage-related activities and of failing to meet certain disclosure and reporting requirements. Per the agreement, WCL did not admit to the allegations nor any wrongdoing. Meanwhile, Rocket Mortgage and Mr. Cooper Group recently agreed to pay a combined $6.75 million to the New York State Department of Financial Services to resolve allegations of cybersecurity violations tied to data protection, risk assessments and incident reporting. items.title: New York Governor signs new rules for private listings into law, Compass praises it
items.description: New York’s governor has joined the growing lists of state lawmakers enacting laws to govern the use of private listing networks. On Friday, Governor Kathy Hochul signed Senate Bill S10274, also known as the “ Fair and Transparent Real Estate Listings Act ,” into law, just seven days after it was delivered to her desk. The legislation was first introduced in mid-March before going on to pass the Assembly in late May and the state Senate on June 1, 2026. The law requires residential listings to be publicly advertised or marketed on platforms that are accessible to the general public. According to the law, this means that the publication, platform or website the listing is advertised on does not require payment or for the consumer to work with a certain brokerage or agent in order to view the property information. Additionally, the law specifies that any licensed real estate broker or agent working with a buyer without limitation to a particular brokerage, franchise, or select group of licensees should also be able to view information about the listing. Here's how it will impact real estate professionals and brokerages: Despite this emphasis on ensuring listing information is easily accessible, the law does note that sellers who sign a state-provided standardized disclosure form explaining the risks and tradeoffs associated with non-public marketing, may withhold their listing from public marketing. In the disclosure included in the text of the law, sellers must acknowledge that their property “may not be marketed or distributed outside the real estate brokerage that the listing agent is associated with through mass-marketing channels,” and that due to this, the seller understands that the reduced exposure of the property may lead to a reduction in the number of offers they receive, potentially negatively impacting their ability to sell the house. Those who break this law can be fined up to $5,000. In addition, under the law, the Department of State may suspend or revoke a real estate professional’s license. The law is set to go into effect in late May 2027. Brokerage executives praise law Bess Freedman, the CEO of New York City-based Brown Harris Stevens , a RealTrends Verified brokerage, is celebrating the passage of the law. “Buying a home shouldn’t depend on who you know or which brokerage you work with. I’m proud that New York is taking on private listing networks and making public marketing the standard,” Freedman wrote in an emailed statement. “Buyers deserve to see what’s available and choose who represents them. Sellers deserve the chance to reach the widest possible audience, and those who want privacy — a choice that has always existed — can still choose it with a clear understanding of what they may give up.” In addition to Freedman, Caroline Burton , the general manager of StreetEasy , which is owned by Zillow , is also applauding the news and thanking the state legislature for “putting consumers first.” “When homes are kept out of public view, New Yorkers lose out, especially in a market where homes for sale are already scarce,” Burton wrote in an emailed statement. “Finding a home in the most challenging market shouldn’t depend on privilege, who you know or who you work with. In one of the biggest decisions in a person’s life, New Yorkers deserve an open and transparent marketplace so they can make an informed choice. This is a win for all buyers, sellers, and the agents who serve them.” Compass excited about homeowner choice Beyond these two firms, which had been vocal proponents of listing transparency, Compass International Holdings, which has been promoting its three-phased marketing plan , which includes a private listing phase , is also praising the enacting of the law . A Compass spokesperson told HousingWire that the new law “preserves homeowners’ right to choose how they market their homes,” which includes marketing the property through Compass's See It First initiative. Compass launched See It First in September . The company said it is intended to expand inventory visibility for buyers, allow sellers to “test and learn ” without public days on market and provide agents with an additional marketing lever. “See It First early access homes comply with the new law and continue to give sellers flexibility in how and when they bring their homes to market,” a Compass spokesperson told HousingWire via email. Similarly, the New York State Association of Realtors (NYSAR) said in a statement that the "legislation strikes an appropriate balance between promoting transparency and protecting consumer choice by preserving the ability of property owners to determine how their properties are marketed." "This new law helps ensure that property owners are fully informed of the potential consequences of limiting the public marketing of their properties, including the possibility of reduced exposure to prospective buyers or tenants," the statement read. Other states weigh in on private listings In enacting this law, New York is joining Connecticut , Wisconsin and Washington in creating a law governing the public marketing of residential properties. New York’s law is similar to the ones passed in Connecticut and Wisconsin, both of which provide sellers the ability to opt-out of public marketing with a signed disclosure. The Washington law, however, does not include a pathway for sellers to opt-out of public marketing besides a health or safety concern. These laws are currently in effect in Connecticut and Wisconsin, with Washington's law slated to go into effect on Jan. 1, 2027. Related More: Brown Harris Stevens Clear Cooperation Co Compass

items.title: Non-QM lending grows as buyers change financing strategies
items.description: Homebuyers are increasingly willing to change their mortgage financing strategies to get into the housing market, helping drive growth in nonqualified mortgage ( non-QM ) lending according to new research from Cotality . Data presented during a Cotality webinar last week found that 69% of buyers initially cut lifestyle spending to make homeownership more affordable. But once these adjustments become insufficient, 65% turn to changing their financing options, according to the company's analysis of homebuyer behavior. The findings point to growing demand for alternative mortgage products. "The economy and the way people earn income has changed," said Selma Hepp , chief economist at Cotality. "Non-QM is becoming a permanent component of the mortgage market because the borrower base it serves is permanent." Hepp pointed to the growing number of business owners, independent contractors, commission-based workers, real estate investors and households with multiple income sources. She cited approximately 11.9 million independent contractors, representing 7.4% of employment, and 9 million multiple-job holders, representing 5.5% of employed people. Many of these borrowers may have the financial resources to repay a mortgage but struggle to demonstrate their income through conventional underwriting. But Hepp cautioned that alternative underwriting should not be presented as a simple affordability solution. “What it can do is align underwriting more closely with what the borrower’s actual financial capacity is,” she said. Nonagency lending has expanded in recent years, driven primarily by non-QM loans, said Patrick Kaiser, Cotality’s principal product manager in property intelligence. Kaiser said non-QM lending was on pace to exceed 2025 volume by the end of 2026 and could grow again in 2027 if current trends continue. Loans for consumer borrowers remain the largest share of the market, but debt-service-coverage ratio ( DSCR ) loans for real estate investors are gaining ground. Investor activity Investor lending brings its own risks. Rising insurance premiums, property taxes and other operating costs can weaken rental-property cash flow, Hepp said. A softer labor market could also put pressure on borrowers with self-employment or variable income. But Holly Niemeier , a senior loan officer at NEXA Lending who works primarily with investors, told HousingWire that investor demand has kept her busy despite elevated borrowing costs. Her clients range from first-time investors to those with hundreds of properties, including some looking to acquire as many as 20 at a time. "People are having a hard time getting loans, and the investors now, the prices have dropped some, so I'm busier than I've ever been this month," she said. "The rates aren't really affecting the investors. They're still buying." Niemeier said investors use different strategies depending on their available capital. Some buy properties with cash, renovate them and refinance, while others purchase turnkey rentals with existing tenants. Those who run low on capital may use hard money loans to acquire and renovate properties before refinancing into DSCR loans. Virtually all of Niemeier’s investor business involves DSCR financing, either for individual properties or through portfolio loans. She also sees investors favoring lower-cost properties in urban markets such as St. Louis and Detroit, where smaller down payments can make it easier to expand a portfolio. "The investors don't seem to flinch," she said. "They don't change anything." Related More: Cotality NEXA Lending Non-QM Real Estate Investing

items.title: Real estate reputation is built through consistency and culture
items.description: Every brokerage can rank its agents by volume . Far fewer can say what clients will remember about working with them five years later. Sales volume and record-breaking transactions are meaningful measures of success. But after more than two decades in real estate, I've learned that they capture only the result, not the experience behind it. They don't tell us whether an agent gave difficult advice at the right moment, brought the right people together or earned the kind of trust that leads to the next relationship. We often talk about reputation as something an individual agent builds. In reality, it's something an entire team has to deliver. The standard is in the details In luxury real estate , exceptional service is sometimes mistaken for extravagant gestures. More often, it comes down to something quieter: preparation, discretion, good judgment and following through on commitments. Consistency doesn't mean giving every client an identical experience. It means maintaining the same standards while understanding what matters to each person. One seller may want absolute privacy ; another may expect detailed updates after every showing. In New York City, where clients have many options and high expectations, candor matters just as much as polish. Sometimes the best service is telling a seller their home needs to be priced correctly from day one, rather than offering an appealing number that won't stand up to the market. That conversation won't appear in a production ranking. But it may be the reason the client calls again. Reputation is a team effort An agent leads the relationship, but the client encounters the work of many people. Photography, staging, marketing, operations and strategic partnerships all shape the experience and ultimately an agent's reputation. As a leader, I believe one of our most important responsibilities is creating an environment where agents have the resources, relationships and collaborative support to build exceptional businesses. The strongest agents aren't operating in isolation. They're surrounded by people who share their commitment to exceptional service. Our recent relaunch of The Elysia at 200 East 59th Street is one example. Working alongside agents Michael Biryla and John Antretter and our partners at rennie, The Agency's New York marketing and creative teams helped reintroduce the condominium with a refreshed identity and cohesive strategy. From the property's positioning and creative materials to its September relaunch event, each element reflected a shared vision. The result demonstrated how different areas of expertise can come together to create a cohesive client experience. That's the distinction between generating attention and earning confidence. When agents have a team working toward a common goal, they're better equipped to deliver the thoughtful service that strengthens relationships over time. Growth tests the promise It's one thing to deliver a memorable experience once. It's another to maintain that standard as a brokerage grows. A brand isn't built by placing the same logo in more markets, nor is success defined solely by adding agents or offices. Meaningful growth comes from building a culture where people feel supported, collaboration is encouraged and the client experience remains exceptional regardless of location. Throughout my career, I've learned that culture isn't established through messaging alone. It's reflected in how teams communicate, share knowledge and support one another. That means recognizing the marketers, operations professionals and specialists whose contributions strengthen agents' businesses. Local expertise and individual character remain essential, but the same standards of professionalism, discretion and care should be reflected throughout the organization. Reputation is built over time Reputation is rarely defined by a single transaction. It's built through years of consistent decisions, meaningful relationships and sound guidance when clients need it most. In challenging markets, when buyers are selective and sellers face difficult decisions, clients rely on advisors who communicate honestly and guide them through uncertainty. Having difficult conversations, adjusting strategies and prioritizing clients' long-term interests are what ultimately build lasting trust. As leaders, our responsibility is to create a culture that reinforces those values and gives agents the support to uphold them. Production should be celebrated, but we should also recognize the repeat clients, referrals, collaboration and sound judgment that make it sustainable. The question isn't simply who had the biggest year. It's who has built an experience, and a team, that people will trust again. That's the kind of success that lasts. items.title: Trump Threatens 'Tremendous Tax' On Companies Building Data Centers Abroad
items.description: U.S. companies that build data centers internationally will face a “tremendous tax,” President Donald Trump said Friday, in a new push for more domestic data center construction. Flickr/The White House/Andrea Hanks President Donald Trump Trump’s attempt to discourage the building of facilities outside of the U.S. comes weeks after voters overwhelmingly rejected data centers as an issue during the midterm elections. “We’re going to fight very hard for the data centers,” Trump said at a White House press conference . If companies choose to keep building data centers outside the country, Trump said they can, but they will face a “tremendous tax.” He hadn’t yet informed his staff of the policy, saying he was telling his people now. Even before the election, in which voters chose multiple new governors who promised to implement development moratoriums, getting approval for U.S. data center projects had become more challenging. Local opposition blocked or delayed nearly $68B of projects in the second quarter. New York Gov. Kathy Hochul in July ordered a one-year moratorium on large data centers, halting about $10B of development. Only 13% of registered voters said they would support an artificial intelligence data center within 10 miles of their home, according to a CNBC survey , while 64% of respondents opposed the notion. But the world’s largest tech companies are pouring billions of dollars each into the AI build-out, with J.P. Morgan estimating that hyperscalers like Amazon and Meta will spend $700B on data centers in 2026 alone. “We have a lot of places that want them badly, and they’re great places,” Trump said during the Friday press conference. “They have energy, and they have everything. They’re tremendous assets.” American tech giants like Alphabet , Microsoft and Oracle have already built facilities internationally. Global investors have also been drawn to Europe's slow and steady approach to data center regulation as U.S. rules have become unpredictable. Trump’s comments came a day after he met with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Xi congratulated Trump on “how well we’re doing” in AI, Trump said. items.title: Ardstone Launches €169M Dublin Housing Venture With ISIF And CBRE IM
items.description: Courtesy of Ardstone Ardstone's Barn Oaks, part of its expansion programme Dublin residential investor and developer Ardstone has launched a €169M housing venture with the Ireland Strategic Investment Fund and CBRE Investment Management . CBRE IM is investing through its Indirect Private Real Estate Strategies platform, alongside ISIF, while the Ardstone Residential Income Fund also holds a direct equity stake, with Ardstone co-investing. The venture is the first phase of ARIF's development programme and provides another route for the fund to originate and deliver new homes, rather than relying solely on acquiring completed residential assets, Ardstone said. Ardstone owns and operates approximately 3,100 homes across 21 assets in the Greater Dublin Area, with a gross asset value of approximately €1.4B. The new capital will support its ambition to grow ARIF to approximately 5,000 homes and €2B in gross asset value in the near term. The fund also has longer-term potential to reach approximately €3B, subject to investment opportunities and market conditions. “Our ability to scale is not dependent on competing for a limited pool of completed assets," Ardstone CEO Donal O’Neill said in a statement. "Our specialist focus on Irish residential gives us the development capability, local relationships and origination network to create our own pipeline and match new institutional capital with identified opportunities.” The investment also gives CBRE IM's clients exposure to the Irish residential market, where population growth and a persistent housing shortage continue to underpin demand. “Through our partnership with Ardstone, we are able to access high-quality, development-ready opportunities while benefiting from a disciplined structure designed to deliver attractive risk-adjusted returns,” CBRE IM Indirect Private Real Estate Strategies Head of EMEA Living Investments Line Verroken said in a statement. Ardstone operates as a vertically integrated Irish residential investment and development platform, covering investment and development management, fund management, finance and residential operations. Its in-house operating business, Storyhouse, manages leasing, apartment turnover and resident services, providing operational data to inform asset management and investment decisions. items.title: Jensen Huang's Return To Nvidia Revives Bets On Data Center Funding
items.description: Jensen Huang , one of the leading figures behind the artificial intelligence data center boom, is back on top at Nvidia following a push from the White House. Nvidia Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang The chipmaker's board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang as president and CEO, it announced Monday morning . Huang had resigned Nov. 12 following reports that he had an affair with a data center executive whom U.S. intelligence suspected of spying for China, as well as reports of additional affairs with two employees. The board said Monday its investigation into the reports of a foreign intelligence effort is ongoing. But it received "input from senior levels of the United States government" that gave it confidence that reinstating Huang wouldn't pose a risk to national security. “The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” Nvidia Chair Harvey Jones said in a statement. President Donald Trump , who had called for Huang's reinstatement, said in a statement Monday morning that the board made the "correct and proper decision." "The Country needs Jensen's leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy," Trump said in a Truth Social post . Nvidia's stock price jumped more than 30% when the market opened Monday. Its price had fallen more than 20% last week after Huang's resignation — and 40% over the past month since the scandal came to light — despite the company posting quarterly earnings Tuesday that beat forecasts. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress, who took over as interim CEO, voiced confidence on its earnings call that the company remained "business as usual" and that Nvidia's "customers and partners are with us." Huang said Tuesday ahead of the earnings report that he was open to returning as CEO after receiving "an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers." In Monday's release, Huang thanked the board, Jones and Kress, and said he takes "this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment." “I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” Huang said in the statement. The AI revolution Huang has championed has created unprecedented demand for data centers and led to a wave of development across the country. Over the past year, Nvidia expanded from being the lead supplier of chips to those data centers to being a financial backer that supported several aspects of the data center development ecosystem. It has funded fast-growing neocloud AI firms like CoreWeave and Nebius that are gobbling up chips and data center space. And it has served as a financial backstop to AI data center operators, promising to cover tens of billions in leases if they can't pay. Nvidia said last week it had $118B in guarantees outstanding, including a $105B deal for an OpenAI campus in Ohio being developed by SB Energy on land leased from the federal government . Kress had said on Tuesday's earnings call that Nvidia would honor its current commitments and would continue to provide support to the neocloud sector but would be "disciplined and selective in our support." CoreWeave's stock fell more than 4% after Nvidia's earnings report, but it jumped more than 25% Monday morning after Huang's reinstatement, signaling that Wall Street believes he will be more aggressive in funding the sector. Huang had also been working with Wall Street's biggest firms to fund the AI data center build-out. In August, he received pledges from Apollo Global Management , BlackRock , Blackstone , Brookfield , Goldman Sachs and KKR to deploy at least $500B for the development of AI infrastructure. The Wall Street Journal reported last week that no capital had yet been deployed in that effort and that investors were "increasingly skeptical" that the initiative would achieve its ambitions without Huang leading Nvidia. It remains to be seen how quickly dealmaking will resume with Huang back at the helm. recent_coverage.summary_zh: HousingWire 专栏作者认为，需求不足使住宅建设许可接近疫情时期低位；Census 显示，10 月许可年化为 1,295,000 套，较前一月修订值 1,398,000 下降 7.4%。

recent_coverage.title: Bank Branch Costs Hinge More on Market Than Management, JLL Finds
recent_coverage.summary_zh: JLL 报告称，美国银行 2026 年上半年新开网点数量超过关闭数量；其研究指出，12 个市场中每平方英尺设施运营成本最高与最低相差 2.6 倍。

recent_coverage.title: Mortgage Rates Move Slightly Lower
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 平均高等级 30 年固定利率为 7.46%，连续第 2 天回落；但较上周初高近 0.20%，报道认为 11 月下半月利率可能受假日交易影响而波动。

recent_coverage.title: October 2026 Rental Report: Rents Rise Annually for the First Time Since June 2023
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Realtor.com 称 10 月中位挂牌租金为 $1,692，较上年同期上升 $1（+0.1%），为 2023 年 6 月以来首次同比上涨；2026Q3 完工量和新开工分别为 330,000 和 403,000，同比下降 26% 和 9.2%。

recent_coverage.title: BTR Operators Push For Treasury To Loosen Rules As Consolidation Looms
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 拟议财政部规则要求持有至少 350 套单户出租房的机构投资者先制定书面 BTR 计划，并限制证书签发 18 个月后购入房屋；运营商称或压制资本流入和新建社区。

recent_coverage.title: Fitch warns of growing balance-sheet strain at top nonbank mortgage firms
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Fitch 将 Pennymac、Planet 和 Freedom Mortgage 的长期发行人评级展望由稳定调为负面，称高杠杆和 MSR 暴露拖累信用状况，2027 年盈利或受利率环境约束。

recent_coverage.title: Pending Home Sales Decreased 4.7% in October, According to NAR Report
recent_coverage.summary_zh: NAR 报告显示，10 月住宅签约量环比下降 4.7%、同比下降 16.7%，四大区域均下滑；首席经济学家称连续两个月创纪录低位或预示第四季度成屋销售收官疲弱。

recent_coverage.title: Sherwood Equities Sells Hudson Yards Development Site For $100M: The N.Y. Deal Sheet
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Sherwood Equities 将 460 10th Ave. 的 17K SF 住宅开发地块以 $100M 售予 Joyland Group；买方与 Prospect Development 计划建设 34 层、456 套公寓，卖方出售原因不明。

recent_coverage.title: New Residential Construction Press Release
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Census 显示，10 月新屋开工年化季调后为 1,309,000，较 9 月修订值上升 9.9%、同比上升 2.8%；营建许可为 1,295,000，较 9 月修订值下降 7.4%、同比下降 8.7%。

recent_coverage.title: New Home Lot Supply Index
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Zonda 的 New Home Lot Supply Index 在 2026Q3 升至 88.5，同比上升 20.8%、较 2Q26 上升 3.9%，市场评级转为“供应适当”；研究机构提醒，可负担性压力、激励措施及土地成本挑战仍在。

recent_coverage.title: HUD finalizes rule targeting mixed-immigration-status households receiving aid
recent_coverage.summary_zh: HUD 于 11 月 12 日最终确定新规，要求住房援助家庭所有成员证明美国公民身份或合资格移民身份；规则 12 月 14 日生效，NLIHC 估计或影响多达 80,000 人，相关诉讼已提起。

recent_coverage.title: Fed Officials Expect Further Interest Rate Hikes After Pausing Last Month
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 10 月 FOMC 以 10 比 2 维持隔夜利率 3.75%--4%；纪要称部分官员认为未来加息可能适宜，少数人考虑 12 月更大幅度加息，CME FedWatch 显示半个百分点加息概率为 5%。

recent_coverage.title: Morgan Completes 345-Unit Multifamily Project in North Austin
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Morgan 完成北奥斯汀 The Watson 多户项目，共 345 套，建筑为 7 层，含单间及一至三居室；工作室租金起价约 $1,600／月，项目配有泳池、健身中心和共享办公空间。

recent_coverage.title: IPA Negotiates Sale of 399-Unit Apartment Community in Grapevine, Texas
recent_coverage.summary_zh: IPA 代表 Greystar 出售德州 Grapevine 的 The Preserve 公寓社区；项目建于 2020 年，共 399 套，平均面积 968 SF，买方未披露。

recent_coverage.title: HOUSTON RENTERS KEEP THE MARKET MOVING IN OCTOBER
recent_coverage.summary_zh: HAR 称 10 月休斯敦地区单户住宅出租 3,850 套，同比增 3.5%，平均租金升至 $2,293；联排与公寓出租量增 9.1%，但库存继续扩张，新挂牌增 1.7%、在售增 3.3%。

recent_coverage.title: MarketBeat SF Bay Area Life Sciences Q3 2026
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Cushman & Wakefield 称，湾区生命科学就业在 2026Q3 为 104,400 个岗位，空置率为 28.5%，季度租赁活动达 828,511 SF；但平均 NNN 要价降至每月每 SF $5.53。

recent_coverage.title: Congress Puts Up $216M For Energy Department Relocation From Forrestal
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 参议院委员会批准 $215.6M，用于能源部员工迁出 1.8M SF 的 Forrestal 办公楼群及新总部准备；GSA 可考虑该楼的其他用途或处置，但尚无时间表。

recent_coverage.title: Griffin Capital Starts Work on 132 Lakeside Village Rental Townhomes
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Griffin Capital 在 Flower Mound 推进 Lakeside Village 的 132 套租赁联排住宅，建设成本预计 $40M，计划于 2028 年 8 月完工；项目占地近 10 英亩，分布于 26 栋建筑。

recent_coverage.title: Kisco Senior Living Lands $52M Refi on San Rafael Senior Living Community
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Kisco Senior Living 为 San Rafael 的 123 套老年社区获得 $52.2M Freddie Mac 再融资，期限 10 年、全期只付息并含现金提取；物业过去 24 个月入住率保持在 91% 以上。

recent_coverage.title: Partners Capital Acquires Terraces at Windward Retail Center in Metro Atlanta
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Partners Capital 收购亚特兰大都会区 84,620 SF 的 Terraces at Windward，物业售出时有 14 个租户；该基金计划首年投入超过 $1M，改造外立面及停车场。

recent_coverage.title: October 2026 multifamily starts and permits signal a potential shift in supply outlook
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Zillow 称 10 月全国多户新屋开工升至 433,000 套，较 9 月上升 25.5%；多户许可降至 475,000，较 9 月下降 5.2%，但全国租客需求同比增 22.1%，买方需求仍弱。

recent_coverage.title: Homeownership Remains a Key to Household Wealth
recent_coverage.summary_zh: NAHB 引述美联储 SCF 称，2025 年美国自住住宅合计价值 $47.2 trillion，占家庭总资产 26%；66% 家庭拥有自住住宅，报告强调住房对财富积累与家庭财务安全的重要性。

recent_coverage.title: Mortgage rates jump to 7.58% as inflation lifts bond yields
recent_coverage.summary_zh: HousingWire 数据显示，周二美国 30 年期合规按揭平均利率为 7.58%，较一周前上升 23 个基点。报道指出，通胀和债券收益率上行，抵消了近期购房负担能力的部分改善。

recent_coverage.title: Zillow: CPI Shelter Forecast, November 2026
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Zillow 将 2026 年末租金同比涨幅预测从 3.06% 下调至 3.04%，将业主等价租金预测从 3.44% 上调至 3.53%，并指出年末住房通胀回升部分源于统计调整。

recent_coverage.title: Perennial Housing launches as affordable owner, operator
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 获机构资本支持的 Perennial 在美国东南部和中西部收购 31 处物业，覆盖 10 个州、近 4,000 套公寓。据公司披露，97% 的公寓获项目型 Section 8 租赁援助合同支持。

recent_coverage.title: Austin Office Campus Lands $228M Refinancing Deal
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 奥斯汀甲级写字楼园区 Springdale Green 获得 2.275 亿美元 C-PACE 绿色融资，置换原建设贷款。融资方 Nuveen 称，这是得州迄今规模最大的同类交易。

recent_coverage.title: A Better Credit Score Could Save Buyers $864 a Year on a Typical Mortgage
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Zillow 测算，2026 年 10 月购买美国典型住宅并首付 20% 时，信用评分 740 分及以上的买家，相比低于 680 分的买家，每年可少付 864 美元。

recent_coverage.title: HSBC Sells $300M Of Data Center Debt Tied To Stargate Project At Big Discount
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 据彭博社报道，汇丰以每美元面值不足 90 美分的价格出售 Jupiter 项目 3 亿美元建设债务。若项目延期或无法推进，甲骨文可依据已发出的不可抗力通知推迟付款。

recent_coverage.title: A conflict of interest
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Cotality 指出，机构投资回撤之际，小型投资者借助非合格按揭扩大住宅投资，5 年期仅付息贷款可改善短期持有的租赁利润；该机构认为，投资需求使房价和租金维持高位。

recent_coverage.title: Multifamily Rebalancing Advances
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 高力国际称，2026 年第 3 季度美国多户住宅入住率升至 95.7%，净吸纳低于新增交付，开发管线继续收缩；60 个主要市场中有 40 个租金同比上涨。

recent_coverage.title: Builder Sentiment Continues to Fall on Affordability Concerns
recent_coverage.summary_zh: NAHB 与富国银行的 11 月住房市场指数下降 4 点至 25，为 2012 年 4 月以来最低。调查显示，46% 的建商降价，68% 提供销售优惠；NAHB 指出，建商正在缩减施工规模。

recent_coverage.title: MarketBeat SF Bay Area Multifamily Q3 2026
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 戴德梁行称，2026 年第 3 季度旧金山湾区多户住宅空置率连降 12 个季度至 3.9%，季末有效租金同比上涨近 10%，在建量连续第 5 个季度上升至 18,625 套。

recent_coverage.title: Onyx+East, EJF Capital to Develop $17.5M Build-to-Rent Community in Indianapolis
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Onyx+East 与 EJF Capital 敲定合资开发，总投资 1,750 万美元的 Monon 21 将建 57 套出租住宅。项目已完成拆除并开始场地准备，计划于 2028 年底完工。

recent_coverage.title: LAHSA To Return $150M Of HUD Funding In Finalized Settlement
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 联邦法官签署和解协议，要求洛杉矶无家可归者服务管理局退还约 1.5 亿美元联邦资金。资金将分阶段转由洛杉矶县管理，地区每年 2.4 亿美元的住房服务拨款申请得以保留。

recent_coverage.title: Promise Robotics raises $25M to scale automated homebuilding
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Promise Robotics 宣布获 2,500 万美元 B 轮融资，此前已与 D.R. Horton 签订多年协议，支持其建造超过 1,250 套住宅。公司计划于 2027 年启用凤凰城工厂。

recent_coverage.title: Custom Home Building Share Rises in 2025
recent_coverage.summary_zh: NAHB 援引美国人口普查局调查称，定制住宅占独栋住宅开工的比重从 2024 年的 17.5% 升至 2025 年的 19.6%；2025 年开工的独栋住宅中，8.6% 为出租而建。

recent_coverage.title: Westcore Entity Pays $51.1M for Seattle-Area Light Industrial Campus
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Westcore 关联实体从黑石旗下 Link Logistics 收购西雅图以东伍丁维尔的一处多租户轻工业园，交易金额据报道为 5,110 万美元。

recent_coverage.title: New-Construction Insights: Builders Hold Steady on Price, but Offer Savings via Reduced Rates
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Realtor.com 称，美国新屋挂牌中位价近 3 年基本持平。按房价 40 万美元、首付 10% 测算，得益于利率优惠，新屋买家首年利息平均每月比典型成屋买家少 258 美元。

recent_coverage.title: Big V Property Group Acquires 7.4-Acre Parcel in Anna, Texas, for Retail Expansion Project
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Big V 在达拉斯以北的安纳收购 7.4 英亩地块，紧邻其在建购物中心 Rosamond Town Center，并从一家地区银行获得 1,100 万美元收购及建设贷款。

recent_coverage.title: First liens may lag until 4Q27 as cash-outs, seconds compete
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 据 National Mortgage News 报道，房利美虽将按揭利率预测下调至 7.2%，仍预计按揭业务量疲弱将持续至 2027 年第 3 季度，部分放贷机构正转向第二顺位按揭。

recent_coverage.title: ARCTRUST, Edison Equity Break Ground on 175-Unit Active Adult Community in Metro Austin
recent_coverage.summary_zh: ARCTRUST 与 Edison Equity 在奥斯汀西南部启动 Serenova 长者社区建设。项目共 175 套住宅，面向 55 岁及以上住户，计划于 2028 年秋季完工。

recent_coverage.title: FASB rule could push community banks to sell servicing
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 据 National Mortgage News 报道，美国财务会计准则委员会拟议的会计标准可能使部分金融机构更难评估按揭服务权价值，社区银行或因此出售相关服务权。
